name: ACL OCL Corpus
description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. Integrating and enhancing the previous versions of the ACL Anthology, the ACL OCL contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar). The ACL OCL spans seven decades, containing 73K papers, alongside 210K figures.
creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
publisher: National University of Singapore, Pennsylvania State University
citeAs: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan. 2023. The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics. arXiv:2305.14996v2 [cs.CL]
rai:dataCollection: We start by crawling the PDF files and metadata from the source ACL Anthology. We design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website. We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks. We then obtain 73,285 conference journal and workshop papers in the CL domain. The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology. For these updates, we identify new additions by monitoring changes in URLs.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website (https://aclanthology.org/). The ACL Anthology digitally archives all scientific papers in the CL domain, including metadata, PDF files, and supplementary materials.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We pass the PDF files through the full-text extraction process using GROBID for the full-text extraction from PDF files. We take the S2ORC-JSON format used by Lo et al. (2020) and Wang et al. (2020) for our full-text schema, which includes complete information parsed from PDF files, such as metadata, authors, and body text with citations, references, sections and etc. We extract figures and tables from PDF files using PDFFigures (Clark and Diwala, 2016). Each extracted figure is associated with its caption texts, which show the figure ID and textual description in the paper. The figures are stored separately from the textual data in OCL. We use GROBID's metadata extraction, but the OCL uses the metadata from ACL Anthology as it is more accurate given its author-driven nature.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For topic classification, we crawl published papers of several online held CL conferences (e.g., ACL 2020, EACL 2021) between 2020 and 2022, together with their topics from those websites. After aligning those papers with the data in the ACL OCL, we obtained 2545 documents classified in 21 topics in total. We train a pre-trained language model (PLM) based topic classification method on a subset of 2,545 scientific papers with ground truth topic labels. We then extrapolate and integrate the model predictions as silver-labeled topic information in the OCL.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The best performance (achieved by the PLM-based supervised method) is comparable to those reported in the state-of-the-art topic classification tasks on the scientific domain. From the last column in Table 3 (system-predicted topics), we observe 13 correct labels out of 15 documents. Two works in Resource & Evaluation, namely BLEU and ROUGE, are incorrectly predicted due to insufficient training samples and high overlap with other topics. The 87% accuracy is higher than an expected 69% accuracy tested on the STop test set in Table 5, mainly because of the bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics (e.g., MT).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID for full-text extraction from PDF files, PDFFigures for figure and table extraction, language detection toolkit (Shuyo, 2010) for language detection, PLM-based supervised method (SciBERT, SPECTER) for topic classification
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology. For these updates, we identify new additions by monitoring changes in URLs. In the future, we will work on the data currency of OCL, which aims to keep OCL up-to-date with the ACL Anthology data. We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Building scholarly corpora for open research accelerates scientific progress and promotes reproducibility in research by providing researchers with accessible and standardized data resources. The ACL OCL can facilitate the development of document-level information extraction tasks, section-wise tasks such as related work generation, fine-grained linguistic analyses, multimodal research such as figure caption generation, construction of a knowledge graph including papers, authors, topics, datasets, models, claims, and their relationships.
rai:dataBiases: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC, since it does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology. Prior research on the representation of low-resource languages in the ACL Anthology found that numerous languages remain underrepresented. Even among languages in the same language group, there is a significant disparity in coverage.
rai:dataLimitations: Due to the limitations of GROBID in formatting information extraction such as figures, some common issues include missing section names, merged paragraphs, the mixing of footnotes with texts, and misidentifying texts as table captions. GROBID also struggles with the extraction of tables and figures, especially in-line equations. Incorrect metadata such as author names exceeding three tokens, is a common issue. Quantitative assessments show 19 sections are not detected from 21 scientific papers, all footnote numbers are concatenated to the body text with 25 footnotes missing out of 92, 28.78% (19/66) figures not detected, and 76.06% of tables either not detected or detected with wrong contents or titles. The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers and does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology.
rai:dataUseCases: The OCL corpus is designed for open research-oriented applications to serve a wide range of applications including: topic analyses and topic-aided tasks such as emerging topic detection, evolution detection of topics, paper-reviewer matching; tasks that demand complete textual content from scientific papers such as document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific large language models or fine-tuning a general LLM; building scientific assistants for the CL domain; information/knowledge extraction tasks from specific sections such as contribution extraction from Introductions and Conclusions, future work prediction from Conclusions; analysis of historical language change in the CL domain; construction of a knowledge graph including papers, authors, topics, datasets, models, claims, and their relationships; multimodal research tasks such as summarization which integrates text summaries with figures and citation visualizations.
